transformations.description: Uses the complete official EMT stop_code/codParada as the stable Málaga StopNode suffix and creates a same-code singleton StopPlace for each new identity.
Serializes all eight frozen distinct exact GTFS sequences for routes 4, 19 and N3. No sequence in this component is classified as a contiguous short-working variant.
Applies the frozen loop registry exactly. All eight patterns are open in this component; no loop-closing edge is added.
Reuses the accepted canonical es-malaga identity fields exactly and computes only this package-local center/bounds from the 100 routed StopPlace coordinates with deterministic framing padding.
Adds exactly one catalog descriptor and recomputes asset and aggregate SHA-256 values from final serialized bytes.

warnings: The municipal Google Transit ZIP is the frozen topology authority for this snapshot. NAP metadata observed for the same network reports a different trip/calendar snapshot and remains provenance-only because its bytes were not downloaded.

All 100 component coordinates are either exact accepted Grade A objects (35 reused identities) or Grade B official structured municipal GTFS values (65 new identities); no coordinates are inferred or interpolated.
StopNode.sourceReferences is empty because no genuine OpenStreetMap platform or stop_position object was reconciled.

Thirty-five target stop identities are exact-copied from the accepted Málaga baseline and 65 identities are newly created. Later Málaga components must continue to exact-copy accepted StopNode and StopPlace objects whenever IDs recur.
The public code N3 maps to GTFS route_id 43; the public route code is retained in the scenario while source references preserve the GTFS identifier.
Routes CC, L and 20E are preserved in the frozen citywide source registry but excluded from passenger topology because the captured municipal snapshot contains zero trips for them.
